verdict.headline: PPI beats, AAPL hits ATH on China AI approval, but WTI tests $80.58 and September hike probability climbs to 49%
verdict.rationale_short: June PPI printed -0.3% MoM / 5.5% YoY — a second consecutive disinflationary beat — alongside Apple's China AI approval lifting AAPL to a new all-time high (+4%). Morgan Stanley Q2 was a record blowout. Two of three morning conditions met; WTI tested $80.58 intraday (September hike trip wire) before settling near $79.85, and VIX closed at 15.65 — fractionally above the 15.00 BUY threshold. September hike probability rose from 44.5% to 49% on the oil-inflation read-through. TSMC Q2 Thursday at 2pm ET is the week's definitive AI capex resolution event.

Even at close, the WTI $80 level was tested on the highest-conviction Iran escalation day yet (naval blockade + 5th consecutive night of strikes). August CPI will embed this oil shock regardless of where WTI closes today. XLE provides energy FCF exposure and the most direct hedge against September hike repricing.
trade_setups.entry: Increase allocation from 5-6% to 10-12% given the $80 intraday test. Add further to 12-15% if WTI closes above $80 for two consecutive sessions. Reduce to 5% only on confirmed Iran diplomatic resolution with WTI below $70.

bear_case: The WTI intraday test of $80.58 is not dismissible as noise — it is a structural regime signal the HOLD framework partially absorbs but does not fully account for. September hike probability has now risen three days in a row (20% → 44.5% → 49%) driven entirely by energy, and the path to 60% — the threshold that would formally convert HOLD to STEP ASIDE — is shorter than any single disinflation print can offset. The 30Y at 5.10% for four consecutive sessions, refusing to rally through CPI + PPI double-beat, is the bond market explicitly saying it already prices August oil-shock CPI. If TSMC's Thursday print disappoints on H2 AI capex guidance (geopolitical risk to Taiwan, ASML equipment delivery delays, hyperscaler capex guidance revisions), the AI hardware bull thesis re-tests July 8-9 lows in a single session and the Iran + September hike backdrop means no rescue from the macro side. Invalidation: if SPX closes below 7,460 by end of Thursday's session with VIX re-engaging above 17, the HOLD call is wrong — step aside, reduce gross, and wait for August CPI clarity.
